segments.t: As the evening ends, Vika feels obliged to invite German up for coffee after the theater, but German surprises her by politely declining. Meanwhile, Denis and Katya stroll through Moscow eating chocolate ice cream, and Denis wins a lucky prize. Let's listen to the episode finale in Russian.
Можно пригласить его на чашку кофе.
Хотя особого желания у меня нет.
Герман, наш вечер был просто прекрасен.
А кофе на ночь очень вреден.
В отношениях всё бывает как на войне.
Но все главные сражения ещё впереди.
Катя, ты хочешь сейчас мороженое?
Давай, я очень люблю шоколадное.
Здравствуйте, дайте два шоколадных, пожалуйста.
Ты мороженое дашь или оба съешь?
Кажется, я выиграл счастливый билет!
Тогда получай свой приз!
Let's examine the final moments of the episode line by line.
Можно пригласить его на чашку кофе.
'I could invite him for a cup of coffee.' Vika chooses a candid bearing across the room, weaving "mozhno" ("may, can") together with "priglasit" ("to invite") just the way native speakers do.
Хотя особого желания у меня нет.
'Although I have no special desire to.' Vika brings a firm line in this beat, leaning on "osobogo" ("special, particular") before closing the thought with "zhelaniya" ("wish").
Герман, наш вечер был просто прекрасен.
'German, our evening was simply wonderful.' Vika picks a resolute posture at this moment, pairing "vecher" ("evening") with "byl" ("was") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
А кофе на ночь очень вреден.
'And coffee at night is very unhealthy.' Vika chooses a warm bearing in the room, putting "kofe" ("of coffee") alongside "noch" ("night") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
В отношениях всё бывает как на войне.

'In relationships everything can be like in war.' Denis projects a pointed tempo during the exchange, building the phrase around "otnosheniyakh" ("relationships") and "byvayet" ("there can be") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Но все главные сражения ещё впереди.
'But all the main battles are still ahead.' Denis displays a wry line with Vika, linking "glavnyye" ("important"), "srazheniya" ("still"), and "yeshchyo" ("more, still") in one brisk exchange.
Катя, ты хочешь сейчас мороженое?
'Katya, do you want ice cream right now?' Denis questions evenly with Katya now, building the phrase around "khochesh" ("do you want") and "seychas" ("now") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Давай, я очень люблю шоколадное.
'Let's do it, I really love chocolate ice cream.' Katya shows an earnest stance in front of Vika, pairing "davay" ("let's") with "ochen" ("very much") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Здравствуйте, дайте два шоколадных, пожалуйста.
'Hello, give us two chocolate ones, please.' Denis presents an honest style at this moment, pairing "zdravstvuyte" ("hello") with "dayte" ("give") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Ты мороженое дашь или оба съешь?
'Will you give me the ice cream or eat both?' Katya tests wryly during the talk, putting "morozhenoye" ("ice cream") alongside "dash" ("to give") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Кажется, я выиграл счастливый билет!
'It seems I won a lucky ticket!' Denis presents an earnest view beside Katya, building the phrase around "kazhetsya" ("it seems, I think") and "vyigral" ("won") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Тогда получай свой приз!

'Then collect your prize!' Katya strikes a frank attitude as they talk, linking "togda" ("back then"), "poluchay" ("take that"), and "priz" ("prize") in one brisk exchange. Now let's hear the closing scene again without interruption.

Ты мороженое дашь или оба съешь?

Reading the wrapper of his ice cream cone, Denis announces he won a lucky ticket, and Katya rewards him with a passionate kiss. Listen for the command word meaning to collect or receive when you watch the finale. See you next time!
